entries.description: REJECTED my own first golden rather than shipping it. It computed on |b| and negated at the end; the RTL applies sign to the SEED and runs both stages signed, so they differ by an LSB on negatives — 47% of the domain. A golden that disagrees with the artifact on half the domain is not a second opinion, it is a second defect.

THREE OF MY OWN ERRORS, all the same family — confident output from a mechanism that did not do the job: a reference that built silently to nothing and compared against an EMPTY FILE printing 'MISMATCH: 0 differing'; a git push -f to main that was a NO-OP while I reported 'pushed' and CI ran the stock test; and a calibration consuming different cycles than the loop it calibrated, returning exp*256 on all 300 samples. Two caught only because a number was implausible.

Made bar 4 the absolute tapeout contingency — 'run 003 is bar 4 plus nothing'. Building it is what found the wrapper tearing defect. Had the tapeout proceeded on bars 1-3, a die would have been fabricated with an output path whose two bytes could come from different results.

findings.description: BAR 4 FOUND A REAL WRAPPER DEFECT BEFORE TAPEOUT: frame tearing. held updated every 2 cycles on out_valid, so a two-cycle byte read straddled an update and the two bytes could come from different results. Signature: ~77% agreement at every even frame offset, 0% at every odd one — a partial match no alignment can repair is tearing, not misalignment.

The golden model is validated exhaustively against the shipped RTL — 0 mismatches over 8,128 certified-domain inputs, 100% mismatch under +/-1 LSB. It acquits and convicts. First time in this arc the netlist has had a grader with credentials.
